passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: Overview We are one of the leading providers of engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing solutions. We deliver comprehensive design, production, and product management services to companies across a diverse range of industries and end markets. Our capabilities span the entire product lifecycle—from innovation, design, and planning to fabrication, assembly, delivery, and post-production— enabling seamless management of resources and materials across global supply chains. Through these integrated services, we help our customers reduce manufacturing costs, enhance supply chain efficiency, minimize inventory risk, lower transportation expenses, and accelerate product fulfillment. We have three reporting segments: Regulated Industries, Intelligent Infrastructure, and Connected Living and Digital Commerce, which are organized based on the economic profiles of the services performed, including manufacturing capabilities, market strategy, margins, return on capital, and risk profiles. Our Regulated Industries segment is focused on regulated markets and includes revenues from customers primarily in the automotive and transportation, healthcare and packaging, and renewable and energy infrastructure industries. Our Intelligent Infrastructure segment is focused on the modern digital ecosystem including artificial intelligence (“AI”) infrastructure and includes revenues from customers primarily in the capital equipment, cloud and data center infrastructure, and networking and communications industries. Our Connected Living and Digital Commerce segment is focused on digitalization and automation, including warehouse automation and robotics, and includes revenues from customers primarily in the connected living and digital commerce industries. Beginning September 1, 2026, our Connected Living and Digital Commerce segment was renamed to Intelligent Devices and Robotics to better reflect the evolution of the business, including our increased emphasis on automation and robotic capabilities and a strategic shift towards more highly complex, engineered solutions. Our Intelligent Devices and Robotics segment is focused on digitalization and automation, including warehouse automation and robotics, and includes revenues from customers primarily in the connected living and digital commerce and robotics industries. The name change did not impact the composition of the Company's reportable segments or the financial information reported for those segments. Our cost of revenue includes the cost of electronic components and other materials that comprise the products we manufacture; the cost of labor and manufacturing overhead; and adjustments for excess and obsolete inventory. As a provider of turnkey manufacturing services, we are responsible for procuring components and other materials. This requires us to commit significant working capital to our operations and to manage the purchasing, receiving, inspecting, and stocking of materials. At times, we collect deposits from our customers related to the purchase of inventory in order to effectively manage our working capital. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Business and Operational Risks Our ability to schedule production, manage capital expenditures, and maximize the efficiency of our manufacturing capacity is highly dependent on the actions of our customers, who generally do not commit to long-term production schedules and may cancel orders, change production quantities, delay production, and/or change sourcing strategy. Many of our customers do not commit to firm production schedules for more than one quarter. We make significant decisions, including determining the levels of business that we will seek and accept, production schedules and locations, component procurement commitments, personnel needs, and other resource requirements, based on our estimate of customer requirements. Our inability to forecast the level of customer orders with certainty makes it difficult to schedule production and maximize utilization of our manufacturing capacity and supply chain capabilities. Many factors outside of our control impact our customers and their ordering behavior, including recession in end markets, changing technology and industry standards, commercial acceptance for products and shifting market demand, product obsolescence, global pandemics, and loss of business. Customers have canceled their orders, changed production quantities or designs, delayed production, changed their sourcing strategy, and terminated their relationships with us. We cannot assure you that present or future customers will not terminate their service arrangements with us or significantly change, reduce, cancel, or delay the amount of services ordered. Such changes, delays, and cancellations have led to, and may lead in the future to, a decline in our production and our possession of excess or obsolete inventory that we may not be able to sell to customers or third parties. Our ability to recover excess and obsolete inventory costs varies by customer and industry. This has, and may again, result in write downs of inventories, reduction in the number of products that we sell, delays in payment for inventory that we purchased, and reductions in the use of our manufacturing facilities. As many of our costs and operating expenses are relatively fixed, a reduction in customer demand, particularly a reduction in demand for a product that represents a significant amount of revenue, can harm our gross profit margins and results of operations. In the past, we have also been required to increase staffing and other expenses in order to meet anticipated demand. On occasion, customers have required rapid increases in production for one or more of their products or requested that we relocate our manufacturing operations or transfer manufacturing from one facility to another, which stresses our resources and may reduce operating margins. Our business at times experiences periods of rapid growth which can place considerable demands upon our management team and our operational, financial, and management information systems. credit_strengths.text: Gross leverage sits below the sector median and eased year on year, reflecting EBITDA recovery on stronger revenue across the three segments. The balance sheet carries modest net debt relative to earnings, leaving substantial headroom to the next risk-band boundary before leverage becomes a constraint on the credit.

Operating cash flow comfortably covers capital expenditure plus shareholder distributions, and free cash flow alone exceeds buybacks and dividends combined. Internal funding therefore supports the capital programme and returns without incremental borrowing, a meaningful strength for a working-capital-intensive contract manufacturer.

key_risks.text: Customers generally do not commit to firm schedules beyond one quarter, so order cancellations, design changes and sourcing shifts can strand inventory and underutilise relatively fixed capacity. The issuer discloses past write-downs of excess and obsolete inventory, and margin compression from demand shortfalls remains a recurring structural exposure.

The debt stack is laddered with meaningful annual maturities over the coming years, including a sizeable tranche due within the next twelve months. Refinancing is manageable given cash balances and market access, but the schedule concentrates rollover risk in any period of tighter credit or weaker earnings.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage improved year on year and remains comfortably above unity, with EBITDA covering interest several times over. Coverage nonetheless trails the sector median, consistent with thin operating margins typical of turnkey manufacturing rather than any deterioration in the debt structure itself.

Cash flow relative to debt is stable year on year and free cash flow to debt is essentially flat, though both sit modestly below sector medians. Liquidity is the weaker dimension: the current ratio is marginally below one and well under the sector median, so working capital discipline matters for servicing capacity.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is minimal, anchored by leverage well inside the threshold and cash flow coverage of net debt far above the boundary. Our judgement is that the issuer retains considerable capacity to absorb earnings volatility or fund bolt-on acquisitions without breaching tolerance.

Shareholder returns absorb most free cash flow, with buybacks the dominant use, yet operating cash flow still funds capex, distributions and acquisitions together. We view the credit as stable, with the main sensitivities being customer demand concentration, inventory risk and the near-term maturity wall rather than leverage.

credit_strengths.text: 總槓桿低於行業中位數，並按年回落，反映三個業務分部的收入增強帶動 EBITDA 復甦。資產負債表相對於盈利背負溫和的淨債務，距離下一個風險區間邊界仍有充裕空間，槓桿才成為信貸的約束。
營運現金流足以舒適地覆蓋資本開支加股東分派，而自由現金流單獨已超過回購與股息之和。因此內部資金可支持資本計劃及回報，而無需增量借貸，這對營運資金密集的合約製造商而言是重大優勢。

key_risks.text: 客戶一般不會承諾超過一個季度的確定排程，因此訂單取消、設計變更及採購轉移可能令存貨滯留，並使相對固定的產能未能充分利用。發行人披露過往曾就過剩及陳舊存貨計提減值，而需求不足導致的利潤率壓縮仍是反覆出現的結構性風險。
債務結構呈階梯式到期，未來數年有可觀的年度到期債務，包括未來十二個月內到期的一大筆份額。考慮到現金結餘及市場准入，再融資屬可控，但該到期安排會在信貸收緊或盈利轉弱的任何時期集中滾動風險。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率按年改善，並穩固地高於一倍，EBITDA 覆蓋利息數倍。然而覆蓋率仍落後於行業中位數，這與交鑰匙製造典型的微薄經營利潤率一致，而非債務結構本身出現任何惡化。
現金流相對債務按年穩定，自由現金流相對債務基本持平，儘管兩者均略低於行業中位數。流動性是較弱的一環：流動比率略低於一倍，且遠低於行業中位數，因此營運資金紀律對償債能力至關重要。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為極低，錨定於槓桿遠在門檻之內，以及現金流對淨債務的覆蓋遠高於邊界。我們的判斷是發行人保留相當能力吸收盈利波動或為補強型收購提供資金，而不會超出容忍度。
股東回報吸納大部分自由現金流，其中回購為主要用途，但營運現金流仍同時為資本開支、分派及收購提供資金。我們認為該信貸屬穩定，主要敏感因素為客戶需求集中度、存貨風險及近期到期牆，而非槓桿。
